_readme: Seeded practice items -- the FALLBACK for student-005, not the primary path.
Practice is normally generated live for the student's gap; these are what runs
if generation fails validation twice, or if the provider chain is down.
seed.py REFUSES to seed an item whose wrong options match no misconception
pattern for its problem_type. An item like that produces the demo's weakest
moment -- a wrong answer with no diagnosis -- and you would only find out on
stage. If validation rejects something you added, the fix is a distractor that
is a real mistake, not a looser regex.
One item per problem_type, each covering a prerequisite the diagnostic tests.

items.prompt: A class body contains `names = []`. Two objects are created from the class, and the first calls `self.names.append('django')`. What does the second object's `names` contain?
A subclass overrides `__init__()` and does not call `super().__init__()`. What happens to the attributes the parent's `__init__` sets?
A package was installed with pip outside any virtual environment. Inside a freshly created and activated virtual environment, can it be imported?
options: No, the environment has its own packages
Yes, global installs are always available
Only if it is part of the standard library
items.correct_answer: No, the environment has its own packages

items.prompt: A browser sends two separate requests to the same site a moment apart. What does the server remember about the first one when handling the second, if nothing is configured?
A form deletes a comment when it is submitted. Which HTTP method should the form use?
options: POST, because the request changes server state
GET, because it is a simpler request
GET, so the comment id appears in the URL
Either one; the method makes no difference
items.correct_answer: POST, because the request changes server state

items.prompt: A form contains `<input id="title" type="text">` with no `name` attribute. What arrives at the server for that field?
options: The value, keyed by its id
The value, keyed by its type

items.prompt: Two URL patterns in the same file both match an incoming request. Which one handles it?
options: Neither; an ambiguity error is raised

items.prompt: A users table needs a primary key. Which column is the best choice?
One author writes many posts, and every post has exactly one author. Where does the foreign key column belong?
options: On the post table, pointing at the author
On the author table, pointing at the post
items.correct_answer: On the post table, pointing at the author

items.prompt: `Post.objects.filter(id=3)` matches exactly one row. What does it return?
